issues.description: The UML/problem specification defines RollerCoaster.numberOfLoopings as an int and tasks require constructors to accept attributes in the UML order. However, the solution implements RollerCoaster's constructor with a double parameter (public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, double numberOfLoopings)) and casts it to int. This creates a mismatch between the specified attribute type (int) and the constructor parameter type (double), which will confuse students about the expected constructor signature and parameter types.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter types consistent with the UML: change RollerCoaster's constructor to accept an int numberOfLoopings (public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings)) and assign it directly. Update LaunchedRollerCoaster's constructor signature accordingly. Alternatively, if the intention was to use double, update the UML/problem statement and all task descriptions to declare numberOfLoopings as double.
